p2:a.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p2:a: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: J_f(x)=[[2x1,1],[x2,x1]], and J_f(1,2)=[[2,1],[2,1]]. Both have dimensions 2 by 2. p2:b.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p2:b: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: q=2x1^2+x1*x2+x2^2-x1; row gradient=[4x1+x2-1, x1+2x2]; Hessian=[[4,1],[1,2]]. Dimension/multiplication audit: Since A is symmetric, d(1/2 x^T A x)/dx=x^T A. Componentwise differentiation yields the displayed row vector and Hessian. Dimension audit: x,b are 2x1, A is 2x2, q is scalar, and its derivative x^T*A-b^T is 1x2: (1x2)(2x2)-(1x2). The Hessian is the 2x2 matrix defined componentwise by H_ij=partial^2 q/(partial x_i partial x_j), equivalently the Jacobian of (nabla q)^T; it is not inferred by treating the row gradient as a column.

p2:c.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p2:c: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: The stationary point is x*=(2/7,-1/7)^T, and it is the unique global minimizer. Dimension/multiplication audit: Ax*=b. The leading principal minors of A are 4 and 7, both positive, so A is positive definite; q(x)-q(x*)=1/2 (x-x*)^T A (x-x*)>0 for x != x*. Stationarity audit: set the 1x2 row derivative x^T*A-b^T=0_(1x2), hence x^T*A=b^T. Transpose both sides to obtain A^T*x=b, a 2x1 equation; symmetry gives A*x=b. The inverse (2x2) then multiplies b (2x1) on the left.

p3:a.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p3:a: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. p3:b.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p3:b: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. p3:c.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p3:c: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. The last factor integrates to sqrt(3*pi/2), giving Z, which is not 1.

p4:a.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p4:a: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: Phi=[[1,-1],[1,0],[1,1]], Phi^T Phi=[[3,0],[0,2]], and Phi^T y=(5,4)^T. Dimension/multiplication audit: The feature rows are (1,xn). Sum(y)=5, sum(x*y)=4, sum(x)=0, and sum(x^2)=2. Dimension audit: Phi is 3x2, theta is 2x1, y is 3x1, Phi^T*Phi is 2x2, and Phi^T*y is 2x1. This part only forms the design matrices, so no differentiation or transpose of a stationary equation is needed.

p4:b.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p4:b: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: theta_ML=(5/3,2)^T, with predicted mean 17/3 at x*=2. Dimension/multiplication audit: The normal equations are diag(3,2)*theta=(5,4)^T, and (1,2)*theta=5/3+4=17/3. Derivative audit: for J_ML=1/2*||y-Phi*theta||^2, the row derivative is (Phi*theta-y)^T*Phi=theta^T*Phi^T*Phi-y^T*Phi in R^(1x2); products have sizes (1x3)(3x2) and (1x2)(2x3)(3x2). Set it equal to 0_(1x2), giving theta^T*Phi^T*Phi=y^T*Phi. Transpose both sides to obtain Phi^T*Phi*theta=Phi^T*y in R^(2x1), then multiply on the left by the 2x2 Gram inverse.

p4:c.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p4:c: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: theta_MAP=(5/4,4/3)^T, with predicted mean 47/12 at x*=2. The prior shrinks both coefficients toward zero. Dimension/multiplication audit: Noise and prior variances are both 1, so the MAP equations are (Phi^T Phi+I)*theta=Phi^T y, giving diag(4,3)*theta=(5,4)^T. The row gradient of the negative log posterior, up to constants, is theta^T*(Phi^T Phi+I)-y^T*Phi. The intercept is also penalized. Derivative audit: theta is 2x1 and J_MAP=1/2*||y-Phi*theta||^2+1/2*theta^T*theta. Its derivative theta^T*(Phi^T*Phi+I)-y^T*Phi has size 1x2, with the Gram-plus-identity matrix 2x2. Set the row derivative to 0_(1x2): theta^T*(Phi^T*Phi+I)=y^T*Phi. Transpose both sides, using symmetry, to get (Phi^T*Phi+I)*theta=Phi^T*y in R^(2x1). This explicitly includes the intercept penalty.

p5:a.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p5:a: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Subtraction gives the covariance with denominator 3.

p5:b.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p5:b: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. The cross covariance is ordered X then Y as specified.

p5:c.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p5:c: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: Y1 and Y2 are uncorrelated but not independent. Dimension/multiplication audit: Y takes (1,-1),(3,1),(3,-3), each with probability 1/3. Sigma_Y has zero off-diagonal. But P(Y1=1,Y2=-1)=1/3, while P(Y1=1)*P(Y2=-1)=1/9, violating independence.

p6:a.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p6:a: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: y_n|x_1,...,x_N,theta ~ N(theta0+theta1*x_n,sigma^2), and the observations are conditionally independent. Dimension/multiplication audit: With inputs and theta fixed, each observation is a deterministic shift of its own mutually independent Gaussian noise; deterministic shifts preserve independence. Dimension context: theta is 2x1, Phi is Nx2, y is Nx1, and each row phi(x_n)^T is 1x2, so phi(x_n)^T*theta is scalar. This part has no scalar-objective differentiation.

p6:b.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p6:b: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: p(y|Phi,theta)=(2*pi*sigma^2)^(-N/2)*exp[-||y-Phi*theta||^2/(2*sigma^2)]. L(theta)=N/2*log(2*pi*sigma^2)+||y-Phi*theta||^2/(2*sigma^2). Dimension/multiplication audit: Multiply the N scalar Gaussian densities using conditional independence, then take the negative logarithm. Dimension context: Phi*theta and y are Nx1 and their squared Euclidean norm and L(theta) are scalar. Multiplication order in the residual is Phi (Nx2) times theta (2x1). Differentiation and the transpose to normal equations are performed in (d).

p6:c.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p6:c: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: L(theta)=N/2*log(2*pi*sigma^2)+N/(2*sigma^2)*Rhat(theta); they have the same minimizer. Dimension/multiplication audit: Rhat=SSE/N. The additive term does not depend on theta and the multiplier N/(2*sigma^2) is strictly positive. Dimension context: both Rhat and L are scalar functions of theta in R^(2x1); multiplying their row derivatives by the positive scalar N/(2*sigma^2) preserves their 1x2 shape and stationary points. The full stationary and transpose steps appear in (d).

p6:d.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p6:d: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: SSE=y^T*y-2*theta^T*Phi^T*y+theta^T*Phi^T*Phi*theta; its row gradient is 2*theta^T*Phi^T*Phi-2*y^T*Phi. The normal equations are Phi^T*Phi*theta=Phi^T*y. Dimension/multiplication audit: Phi^T*Phi is symmetric. If 'squared error' denotes Rhat rather than SSE, both the expansion and row gradient are divided by N, leaving the same stationary equations. Derivative audit: theta is 2x1, Phi is Nx2, and y is Nx1. The displayed SSE gradient is 1x2: theta^T (1x2) times Phi^T*Phi (2x2), minus y^T (1xN) times Phi (Nx2). Set 2*theta^T*Phi^T*Phi-2*y^T*Phi=0_(1x2), simplify to theta^T*Phi^T*Phi=y^T*Phi, and transpose both sides to obtain Phi^T*Phi*theta=Phi^T*y, a 2x1 equation. Dividing by N for Rhat or by 2*sigma^2 for the theta-dependent NLL does not change this equation.

p6:e.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p6:e: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: theta_ML=(Phi^T*Phi)^(-1)*Phi^T*y is the unique minimizer. Features (1,x,x^2)^T still define linear regression because the prediction is linear in its coefficients. Dimension/multiplication audit: For nonzero h, h^T*Phi^T*Phi*h=||Phi*h||^2>0 by full column rank. Thus the squared-error Hessian 2*Phi^T*Phi is positive definite. Polynomial dependence on input does not change linear dependence on parameters. Dimension audit: (Phi^T*Phi)^(-1) is 2x2 and Phi^T*y is 2x1, so their ordered product yields the 2x1 estimator after the row-zero equation is transposed as in (d). The Hessian is defined by scalar second partials and is 2x2; for Rhat it is (2/N)*Phi^T*Phi and for L it is Phi^T*Phi/sigma^2. With polynomial features, the new parameter is 3x1 and design matrix Nx3; the prediction remains a scalar linear function of these three coefficients. Full rank of the expanded design is not asserted.

p7:a.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p7:a: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: p(theta|y,Phi)=p(y|Phi,theta)*p(theta)/p(y|Phi), proportional to likelihood times prior. The evidence does not depend on theta. Dimension/multiplication audit: p(y|Phi)=integral p(y|Phi,t)*p(t) dt integrates out the dummy parameter t and depends only on y, Phi, and fixed hyperparameters. Dimension context: Phi is NxK, theta and m0 are Kx1, and y is Nx1. The prior and posterior are densities over K-dimensional theta. No scalar derivative is taken in this part.

p7:b.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p7:b: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: -log p(theta|y,Phi)=||y-Phi*theta||^2/(2*sigma^2)+||theta-m0||^2/(2*tau^2)+C, where C=N/2*log(2*pi*sigma^2)+K/2*log(2*pi*tau^2)+log p(y|Phi). Dimension/multiplication audit: Likelihood density is (2*pi*sigma^2)^(-N/2)*exp[-SSE/(2*sigma^2)], and prior density is (2*pi*tau^2)^(-K/2)*exp[-||theta-m0||^2/(2*tau^2)]. The denominator in Bayes' theorem contributes +log evidence to the negative log posterior. Dimension context: Phi*theta-y is Nx1, theta-m0 is Kx1, and each quadratic term is scalar. Their derivatives must therefore be 1xK rows; the ordered products and row-zero/transposition steps are stated in (c).

p7:c.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p7:c: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: The two row gradients are (theta^T*Phi^T*Phi-y^T*Phi)/sigma^2 and (theta-m0)^T/tau^2. MAP satisfies (Phi^T*Phi+(sigma^2/tau^2)*I)*theta=Phi^T*y+(sigma^2/tau^2)*m0. Dimension/multiplication audit: Set the sum of the displayed row vectors to zero, transpose, and multiply by sigma^2. Derivative audit: theta,m0 are Kx1, Phi is NxK, y is Nx1, and both derivatives are 1xK. The likelihood derivative (Phi*theta-y)^T*Phi/sigma^2 has product sizes (1xN)(NxK), equal to [theta^T*(Phi^T*Phi)-y^T*Phi]/sigma^2; the prior derivative (theta-m0)^T/tau^2 is 1xK. Set their sum to 0_(1xK). After multiplying by sigma^2, the row equation is theta^T*(Phi^T*Phi+lambda*I)=y^T*Phi+lambda*m0^T. Transpose both sides and use symmetry to obtain (Phi^T*Phi+lambda*I)*theta=Phi^T*y+lambda*m0 in R^(Kx1).

p7:d.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p7:d: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: theta_MAP=(Phi^T*Phi+lambda*I)^(-1)*(Phi^T*y+lambda*m0), where lambda=sigma^2/tau^2. Dimension/multiplication audit: Multiplying the theta-dependent negative log posterior by 2*sigma^2 gives SSE+lambda*||theta-m0||^2. The penalty includes an intercept if present. Dimension audit: the inverse is KxK and its right-hand vector Phi^T*y+lambda*m0 is Kx1, so the inverse multiplies that vector on the left to produce theta_MAP in R^(Kx1). This solves the column normal equations obtained by transposing the row-zero derivative equation in (c); lambda is scalar.

p7:e.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p7:e: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: Phi^T*Phi+lambda*I is positive definite and hence invertible without any rank assumption on Phi. Dimension/multiplication audit: For every nonzero h, h^T*(Phi^T*Phi+lambda*I)*h=||Phi*h||^2+lambda*||h||^2>0 because lambda=sigma^2/tau^2>0. The associated MAP objective is strictly convex. Dimension audit: h is Kx1, Phi*h is Nx1, and h^T*(Phi^T*Phi+lambda*I)*h is scalar, with multiplication order (1xK)(KxK)(Kx1). The negative-log-posterior Hessian is Phi^T*Phi/sigma^2+I/tau^2, a positive definite KxK second-partial matrix. No new stationary transpose is required after (c).

p7:f.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p7:f: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: For lambda=1 the unique MAP solution is (5/11,5/11)^T. For lambda=0 all pairs with theta1+theta2=1 minimize SSE, so the solution is not unique. As lambda tends to infinity the solution tends to (0,0)^T. Dimension/multiplication audit: Phi^T*Phi=[[5,5],[5,5]], Phi^T*y=(5,5)^T. For lambda>0, theta=(5/(10+lambda),5/(10+lambda))^T. At lambda=1, [[6,5],[5,6]]*(5/11,5/11)^T=(5,5)^T; at lambda=0 only the coefficient sum is identified. Dimension audit: here N=K=2, theta and y are 2x1, and the system matrix is 2x2. For lambda=1 the row stationary equation is theta^T*[[6,5],[5,6]]=[5,5]; setting the row derivative to 0_(1x2) and transposing both sides gives [[6,5],[5,6]]*theta=(5,5)^T. With lambda=0, singularity concerns coefficient uniqueness and does not change derivative orientation.

Dimension/multiplication audit: Each of the two independent likelihood factors and the prior has variance 2 and normalizer 1/sqrt(4*pi). The data inputs are both 1.

p8:b.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p8:b: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: A=3/2, b=3/2, c=5/2. Dimension/multiplication audit: The sum inside the numerator in (a) is 3*theta^2-6*theta+5; dividing by 4 equals (1/2)*[(3/2)*theta^2-3*theta+5/2].

p8:c.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p8:c: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: theta|D ~ N(1,2/3), with posterior density sqrt(3/(4*pi))*exp[-3*(theta-1)^2/4]. Dimension/multiplication audit: A*theta^2-2*b*theta+c=(3/2)*(theta-1)^2+1. The theta-dependent kernel integrates to sqrt(4*pi/3); the constant exp(-1/2) cancels in posterior normalization.

p8:d.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p8:d: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: f*|D ~ N(2,8/3), so its mean is 2 and variance is 8/3. Dimension/multiplication audit: f*=2*theta is a linear transform of a Gaussian: E[f*|D]=2*1 and Var(f*|D)=2^2*(2/3).

p8:e.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p8:e: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: y*|D ~ N(2,14/3), with mean 2 and variance 14/3. Dimension/multiplication audit: The independent future Gaussian noise has mean zero and variance 2; Gaussian sums remain Gaussian, so Var(y*|D)=8/3+2=14/3.

p8:f.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p8:f: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: theta_MAP=1. Fixing theta at MAP gives y*|theta_MAP ~ N(2,2); its variance is 8/3 smaller than the full posterior predictive variance. Dimension/multiplication audit: The posterior is maximized at its mean 1. A fixed parameter contributes no uncertainty; the full posterior predictive adds Var(2*theta|D)=8/3 to the observation-noise variance 2.

p9:a.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p9:a: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: p(y|M_j)=integral N(y|theta,1)*N(theta|0,v_j) dtheta over R. Dimension/multiplication audit: The marginal likelihood averages the conditional sampling density over theta before conditioning on the observed y; the averaging law is the prior. A posterior already conditions on the same observed y and is not the marginalization distribution in this identity.

p9:b.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p9:b: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: p(y|M_j)=[2*pi*(1+v_j)]^(-1/2)*exp[-y^2/(2*(1+v_j))], i.e. y|M_j ~ N(0,1+v_j). Dimension/multiplication audit: (y-theta)^2+theta^2/v=((v+1)/v)*(theta-v*y/(v+1))^2+y^2/(v+1). Multiplying the joint normalizer 1/(2*pi*sqrt(v)) by the Gaussian integral sqrt(2*pi*v/(v+1)) gives the stated normalizer.

p9:c.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p9:c: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: p(0|M1)=1/sqrt(4*pi) and p(0|M2)=1/sqrt(10*pi). Dimension/multiplication audit: The marginal variances are respectively 1+1=2 and 1+4=5; at zero each Gaussian exponential equals 1.

p9:d.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p9:d: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: B12=sqrt(5/2)>1, so the data favor M1 on the Bayes-factor criterion. Dimension/multiplication audit: B12=[1/sqrt(4*pi)]/[1/sqrt(10*pi)]=sqrt(10/4)=sqrt(5/2).

p9:e.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p9:e: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: Posterior odds M1:M2 = B12*(1/3)/(2/3)=sqrt(10)/4. P(M1|0)=sqrt(10)/(sqrt(10)+4), and P(M2|0)=4/(sqrt(10)+4). Select M2 by maximum posterior probability. Dimension/multiplication audit: Dividing Bayes' theorem for the two models cancels their shared data evidence: P(M1|y)/P(M2|y)=[p(y|M1)/p(y|M2)]*[P(M1)/P(M2)]. The odds are below 1, despite B12>1.

p10:a.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p10:a: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. p10:b.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p10:b: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: Phi^T*Phi*theta_hat=Phi^T*y and theta_hat=(Phi^T*Phi)^(-1)*Phi^T*y. Dimension/multiplication audit: Insert r=y-Phi*theta_hat into Phi^T*r=0. Full column rank ensures Phi^T*Phi is invertible because its nonzero quadratic forms equal ||Phi*h||^2>0.

p10:c.evidence: evidence/english-content-review.md row p10:c: Korean and English demands and references agree. Re-read matching solve/verify and recall/pitfall/sum. Independent conclusion agrees: P=Phi*(Phi^T*Phi)^(-1)*Phi^T is a 3 by 3 matrix (generally N by N), with P^T=P and P^2=P. Dimension/multiplication audit: The Gram inverse is symmetric, giving P^T=P.
